questions.question: If log₂x + log₄y = 4 and log₄x + log₂y = 5, what is the value of xy?
questions.solution: Write a = log₂x and b = log₂y. Since log₄ = ½ log₂, the equations are a + b/2 = 4 and a/2 + b = 5, i.e. 2a + b = 8 and a + 2b = 10. So a = 2 and b = 4, giving x = 4, y = 16 and xy = 64.

questions.question: How many integers n satisfy 1 < log₂(log₃ n) < 2?
questions.solution: 1 < log₂(log₃ n) < 2 means 2 < log₃ n < 4, i.e. 9 < n < 81. The integers are 10, 11, …, 80, which is 71 integers.

questions.question: What is the product of all real values of x for which x^(log₁₀x) = 100x?
questions.solution: Take log₁₀ of both sides and write t = log₁₀x: t·t = 2 + t, so t² − t − 2 = 0 and t = 2 or t = −1. Then x = 100 or x = 1/10 (both positive, so both valid), and the product is 100 × 1/10 = 10.

Let f(x) = x/(1 + x) for x > 0, and let fⁿ denote f applied n times (so f²(x) = f(f(x))). What is f¹⁰(1)?
questions.solution: f(f(x)) = (x/(1 + x))/(1 + x/(1 + x)) = x/(1 + 2x), and in general fⁿ(x) = x/(1 + nx), as each step adds x to the denominator. So f¹⁰(1) = 1/(1 + 10) = 1/11.

questions.question: How many functions f from {1, 2, 3, 4} to itself satisfy f(f(x)) = x for every x in the set?
questions.solution: Such an f pairs the elements up and fixes the rest (any element not fixed is swapped with its partner). No swaps: 1 function. Exactly one swapped pair: C(4,2) = 6. Two swapped pairs: 3. Total = 1 + 6 + 3 = 10.

questions.question: For real x, let g(x) = min(2x + 1, x + 4, 7 − x). What is the largest value g(x) can take?
questions.solution: 7 − x falls as x grows while the other two rise, so the maximum of the minimum is where 7 − x meets the smaller rising line. 2x + 1 = 7 − x at x = 2, where both equal 5 and x + 4 = 6 is larger. (Where x + 4 = 7 − x, at x = 1.5, 2x + 1 is only 4.) So the largest value is 5, at x = 2.

questions.question: Section A has 30 students with an average score of 62, and Section B has 45 students with an average of 58. Five students move from A to B, after which A's average rises to 63. What is B's new average?
questions.solution: The five movers' total = 30 × 62 − 25 × 63 = 1860 − 1575 = 285. B's new total = 45 × 58 + 285 = 2610 + 285 = 2895 for 50 students, so its average is 2895/50 = 57.9.

questions.question: A, B and C start a business with capitals in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. After 4 months A doubles his capital, and after 6 months C withdraws half of hers. B's capital is unchanged. Out of a year-end profit of ₹15,300, what is C's share (in ₹)?
In how many ways can 12 be written as a sum of three different positive integers, if the order of the terms does not matter?

A and B take turns, A first. On each of A's turns A rolls a fair die and wins on a six; on each of B's turns B tosses a fair coin and wins on heads. They continue until someone wins. What is the probability that A wins?
questions.solution: A round in which nobody wins has probability (5/6)(1/2) = 5/12. A wins on the first turn of a round with probability 1/6, so P(A) = (1/6)(1 + 5/12 + (5/12)² + …) = (1/6)/(7/12) = 2/7.

questions.question: In a geometric progression with positive terms, the sum of the first three terms is 26 and the sum of the next three terms is 702. What is the fifth term?
questions.solution: The next three terms are the first three multiplied by r³, so r³ = 702/26 = 27 and r = 3. Then a(1 + 3 + 9) = 26 gives a = 2, and the fifth term is 2 × 3⁴ = 162.

questions.question: What is the value of 1×2 + 2×3 + 3×4 + … + 20×21?
A rectangular lawn is 60 m by 40 m. A path of uniform width runs inside it along all four edges, and the path's area is 736 m². What is the width of the path (in m)?
questions.solution: The grass left is (60 − 2w)(40 − 2w) = 2400 − 736 = 1664. Expanding, 4w² − 200w + 2400 = 1664, i.e. w² − 50w + 184 = 0, so w = (50 ± 42)/2 = 4 or 46. The width must be under 20 m, so w = 4.

questions.question: How many non-congruent triangles with integer side lengths have a perimeter of 20?
What is the remainder when 1! + 2! + 3! + … + 100! is divided by 12?
questions.solution: From 4! = 24 onwards every factorial is a multiple of 12, so only 1! + 2! + 3! = 1 + 2 + 6 = 9 matters. The remainder is 9.

questions.question: How many integers from 1 to 1000 are perfect squares or perfect cubes (or both)?
questions.solution: Squares: 1², …, 31² (32² = 1024 is too big), so 31. Cubes: 1³, …, 10³, so 10. Both means sixth powers: 1, 64 and 729, so 3. Total = 31 + 10 − 3 = 38.

questions.question: The roots of x² − px + q = 0 are two consecutive integers. What is the value of p² − 4q?
questions.solution: If the roots are n and n + 1, then p = 2n + 1 and q = n(n + 1). So p² − 4q = 4n² + 4n + 1 − 4n² − 4n = 1. (p² − 4q is also the square of the difference of the roots, which is 1² = 1.)

questions.question: How many real numbers x satisfy x² − 5|x| + 6 = 0?
questions.solution: Since x² = |x|², the equation is |x|² − 5|x| + 6 = 0, so |x| = 2 or |x| = 3. That gives x = ±2 and ±3: 4 solutions.

questions.question: x and y are positive real numbers with x + y = 10. What is the smallest possible value of (1 + 1/x)(1 + 1/y)?
questions.solution: (1 + 1/x)(1 + 1/y) = 1 + 1/x + 1/y + 1/(xy) = 1 + (x + y + 1)/(xy) = 1 + 11/(xy). This is smallest when xy is largest, and with x + y = 10 the largest product is 5 × 5 = 25. So the minimum is 1 + 11/25 = 36/25 = 1.44.

questions.question: Three vertices of a regular octagon are chosen to form a triangle. In how many ways can this be done so that no side of the triangle is a side of the octagon?
questions.solution: Count choices of 3 vertices with no two adjacent. Total C(8,3) = 56. With at least one adjacent pair: a pair of adjacent vertices can be chosen in 8 ways and the third vertex in 6 ways, but the 8 triangles made of three consecutive vertices are counted twice, so 8 × 6 − 8 = 40. Answer = 56 − 40 = 16.

questions.question: What is the value of log₃5 × log₂₅27?
questions.solution: log₃5 × log₂₅27 = (log 5/log 3) × (3 log 3/2 log 5) = 3/2.

questions.question: The average of 20 numbers is 0. At most how many of them can be greater than 0?
questions.solution: Not all 20 can be positive, because then the sum would be positive. 19 can be: take nineteen 1s and one −19, whose sum is 0. So the answer is 19.

questions.question: The 3rd, 5th and 9th terms of a non-constant arithmetic progression are, in that order, three consecutive terms of a geometric progression. What is the common ratio of the geometric progression?
questions.solution: With first term a and difference d ≠ 0: (a + 4d)² = (a + 2d)(a + 8d). Expanding, a² + 8ad + 16d² = a² + 10ad + 16d², so 2ad = 0 and a = 0. The three terms are 2d, 4d and 8d, so the ratio is 2.

questions.question: A positive divisor of 720 is chosen at random, all divisors being equally likely. What is the probability that it is a multiple of 12?
questions.solution: 720 = 2⁴ × 3² × 5 has 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 divisors. A multiple of 12 = 2² × 3 needs the power of 2 to be 2, 3 or 4 (3 ways), the power of 3 to be 1 or 2 (2 ways) and any power of 5 (2 ways): 12 divisors. Probability = 12/30 = 2/5.

questions.question: Two cyclists start at the same time from towns 300 km apart and ride towards each other at 40 km/h and 60 km/h. A drone starts with the first cyclist and flies at 80 km/h back and forth between the two, turning instantly, until the cyclists meet. How many km does the drone fly?
questions.solution: The cyclists close the gap at 40 + 60 = 100 km/h, so they meet after 300/100 = 3 hours. The drone flies the whole 3 hours at 80 km/h, i.e. 240 km. There is no need to add up the individual trips.

questions.question: Two parallel chords of a circle have lengths 16 cm and 30 cm and lie on opposite sides of the centre, 23 cm apart. What is the radius of the circle (in cm)?
questions.solution: Let the 16 cm chord be a cm from the centre and the 30 cm chord (23 − a) cm away. Then r² = 8² + a² = 15² + (23 − a)². So 64 + a² = 225 + 529 − 46a + a², giving 46a = 690 and a = 15. r² = 64 + 225 = 289, so r = 17.
